Hello! Firstly, nice clash, good work :)

I would like to suggest adding a test case (& validator) where all strings are of length 1. This is because for shortest solutions, it's common to read all of input at once, discarding the first line to obtain the list of strings. However, currently you don't actually have to discard it, as the first line is always of length 1, while the answer always has a length of 2+ (or 3+ actually). (Also, given that N is always single-digit in the test cases, I'd suggest changing the constraints to 1 <= N <= 9 or 1 <= N <= 5; this would also make it certain that the first line will always be of length 1 and not possibly 2 with 10 which never actually occurs.)

Thus, adding a test case like
2
A
B
>> A
would make it necessary to discard (or read correctly) the first line.

I do it (Same Length: Test) 🤣

In shortest mode (or even in fastest mode just because) it's common to save quite a few bytes on reading the input, using something like [*open(0)] in python or [*$<] in ruby to get all the lines. This however still grabs the first line (with N, the number of other lines). But currently you can just keep it and solve the problem (with something like max(..., key=len) in python or [...].max_by(&:size) in ruby) as if there was no first line. It's risky though, as you can't know if there is a validator that would break it or not (so like the one I suggested in the previous comment, where this would output "2" instead of "A"). And it's an significant save too, saving you 6+ bytes from a ~30-40 bytes solution, so around 15%--20%.

So no, currently tests do not cover this case, but imho it's important for the shortest mode that they do.

A contribution is marked as Rejected when:
* EITHER 3 reviewers rejects it,
* OR 30 days have passed since it was published (whether as WIP or Ready).

You don't need to delete it. Simply republish the same contribution, and you can continue working on it or try to get it approved (provided you take reviewers' reasonable feedback into account and update the contribution accordingly).

So, are you going to re-create the contribution?

Also, keep in mind that if you leave the contribution's status as WIP, players will never be able to approve it, no matter how much you ask them to.
